findings.title: Negative checks reload full permissions from the DB per resource
findings.body: Check only returns early when the cached permission set allows the request (line 131). Any cache hit that does not allow, and any cache miss, falls through to getIdentityPermissions, and the in-function cache read was removed from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions, so that call always runs GetUserPermissions and reloads the user's full permission set. The new denial cache only suppresses a repeat of the exact same user, action, name, and parent. After that reload refreshes permCache, the next Check for a different resource this user cannot access still misses the denial cache, fails the scope check, and starts another full permission query. singleflight collapses only overlapping calls for the same user and action; once that call returns, the next distinct name queries again. Sequential authz of many dashboards or folders therefore becomes one DB permission load per denied resource per TTL instead of one load per user per action per 30s. In-proc clients now use NoopCache, so they no longer absorb repeats either. Random UIDs (including anonymous GETs) bypass the denial cache and can drive unbounded permission queries. Trust a negative result while the cached permission set is still fresh, and bypass it at most once per TTL rather than once per resource.

findings.title: Denial cache pins non-authoritative denies for 30s and overrides later allows
findings.body: Check returns Allowed=false immediately when permDenialCache contains the key, before consulting cached or current permissions. On any successful deny after the DB path, line 154 stores that denial for shortCacheTTL (30s) and nothing deletes it when a later permission reload would allow the same resource. The denial also wins over a positive permCache entry, so List (which uses the permission cache) can show a resource that Check still denies. This is not limited to authoritative DB denies: checkPermission returns false when the cached folder tree does not yet contain a newly created parent, so an ancestor folder grant is recorded as a denial and keeps failing after the folder cache would have allowed it. getUserPermissions is singleflighted and does not re-read after the in-flight query, so a Check that joins a permission load started before a create/grant can observe the pre-grant snapshot and then pin that stale deny for 30s. That recreates the creator-cannot-open-the-new-dashboard failure, and it extends false denies past permission-cache expiry when a grant follows an earlier deny. Do not write a denial when the result depends on a stale folder tree or a shared in-flight snapshot, and invalidate denial entries whenever permissions are reloaded.

findings.title: Denial cache key collides for UIDs that contain underscores
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with '_' (namespace.perm_<user>_<action>_<name>_<parent>). Dashboard and folder UIDs may contain underscores, and those two fields sit next to each other, so different pairs encode to the same key. For example name "a_b" with parent "c" and name "a" with parent "b_c" both end in _a_b_c for the same user and action. The cache only stores negatives, so a deny for one resource is returned for the other for 30s without checking permissions, and a user who can access one of them is incorrectly denied. Use an unambiguous encoding (length prefixes, a delimiter that cannot appear in UIDs, or a hash).

findings.title: List still serves stale permissions for newly created dashboards and folders
findings.body: List now returns getCachedIdentityPermissions on a hit and only calls getIdentityPermissions on a miss. Check was changed so a cached set that does not include the requested resource is reloaded from the DB, but List still treats the cached set as complete for the whole shortCacheTTL (30s). A creator whose permission cache was filled before the create will not see the new dashboard or folder in list results until that entry expires, which is the failure this PR describes for any caller that fetches via List rather than Check. Use the same freshness rule as Check, or invalidate the permission cache when a dashboard or folder permission is created.

findings.title: Denial-cache test still passes if the short-circuit is removed
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" claims the permission-cache fixture allows dash1 so that only the denial cache can explain the deny. The fixture is map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. checkPermission treats a false or missing scope as not allowed, and setupService's fake store returns no permissions, so Check still returns Allowed=false if the permDenialCache lookup is deleted. The comment says the entry allows access, but the value is false. Set that scope to true and assert the permission store is not called, otherwise a regression of the deny short-circuit is invisible.
